I fixed three bugs in `src/range-tree.js`, each a one- or two-line change. `node --test` passes, and a randomized comparison against a plain array found no differences.

1. **Wrong sums after assign-then-add sequences.** `_applyAssignment` set a new assigned value but kept any pending addition already stored on that node. Later, when those pending updates were passed down to child ranges, the old addition was applied on top of the new value. The documented rule is that assignment happens before addition, so an assignment should cancel earlier additions. The fix clears `_additions[node]` when an assignment is applied. This is the bug the visible test reproduces.
2. **Wrong maxima.** `_max` started its running result at `0` instead of `-Infinity`. Any partly covered range where every value was negative returned `0`. The fix starts it at `-Infinity`.
3. **Wrong threshold-search results.** `_first` moved down into child ranges without first passing pending updates down to them (`_push`). It therefore compared against outdated child maxima, both after an `add` and after an `assign` that hadn't reached the children yet. The fix adds the `_push` call before descending.

The export, API, error handling and empty-range behaviour are unchanged. All operations still run in O(log n) time, construction and `toArray()` in O(n), and storage is still O(n). The search with a starting index visits one path of partly covered nodes, plus at most one fully covered subtree that it descends into and is guaranteed to find a match in.

**Checks run:**
- **Random comparison:** a temporary script ran 3,000 random trees, each 1–40 values long, with 200 random operations per tree. Values were small integers so the sums are exact. It checked `assign`, `add`, `sum`, `max`, `firstAtLeast` (start index up to `length`), `get` and `toArray` against the plain array, including empty ranges, and found no mismatches. I deleted the script afterwards.
- **Test suite:** `node --test` gives 1/1 passing.
